subject: technical-writing
name: Technical Writing
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance).

units.title: Audience, Purpose and the Writing Process
topics: Organise: the pyramid and the outline
Seeing the ideas: tools, manuals, signs and the shape of a message

sections.title: Organise: the pyramid and the outline
Seeing the ideas: tools, manuals, signs and the shape of a message

summary: Technical writing serves the reader's task; qualities are clarity, concision, correctness, completeness, coherence, courtesy and concreteness.
Profile the audience (knowledge, task, environment, language) and state the purpose in one sentence with a verb.
Put the answer first (inverted pyramid), organise by the reader's tasks, use outlines, chunking, lists and tables.
Process: plan, draft, revise, edit and proofread in separate passes, then test with real readers.
Design (headings, warnings, steps, accessibility) is part of the message.

units.title: Style, Clarity and Readability
topics: Common problems in Nepali English writing
Seeing the ideas: scores and sentence surgery

sections.title: Common problems in Nepali English writing
Seeing the ideas: scores and sentence surgery

summary: Write short, active sentences with strong verbs, concrete words, specific numbers and consistent terms; cut deadwood and noun stacks.
Use parallel structure in lists and headings; stay consistent in terms, numbers, dates and units.
Flesch Reading Ease = 206.835 − 1.015(w/s) − 84.6(y/w); FK = 0.39(w/s) + 11.8(y/w) − 15.59; Fog = 0.4[(w/s) + 100(c/w)]. They measure sentence and word length only.
The heavy sentence scores FK 19.0 and Fog 21.7; its seven-word rewrite scores FK 4.0 and Fog 8.5.
Common errors by Nepali writers include articles, over-formal phrases, prepositions and ambiguous dates.

units.title: Software Documentation - SRS, README, API Reference, Runbooks and Postmortems
topics: The documents of a software project
README files, tutorials and user guides
Seeing the ideas: the four kinds of documents and the life of an incident

sections.title: The documents of a software project
README files, tutorials and user guides
Seeing the ideas: the four kinds of documents and the life of an incident

summary: Each document serves a reader at a time: SRS (agree), README (start), guide (do), reference (look up), runbook (respond), postmortem (learn).
Requirements use "shall", one idea each, with testable numbers; vague words (fast, user-friendly, etc.) are defects; a linter can flag them.
A README gets a reader to a first success in minutes; user guides are task-based numbered procedures; error messages say what, why and what to do.
OpenAPI makes API documentation machine-checkable; the example checker found missing summaries and undocumented 4xx responses.
Runbooks give exact steps for on-call; blameless postmortems end in owned, dated action items.

units.title: Research Proposals, Academic Writing and Citation
topics: The structure of a paper or report: IMRaD
Seeing the ideas: the library, the hourglass and two citation styles

sections.title: The structure of a paper or report: IMRaD
Seeing the ideas: the library, the hourglass and two citation styles

summary: A proposal states a specific problem, answerable research questions, a review ending in a gap, a method, scope, timeline and references.
Papers follow IMRaD; a structured abstract has background, objective, method, results with numbers and conclusion.
A literature review synthesises by theme; record sources in a table.
Cite in one consistent style (IEEE numeric, APA author–date); store reference data once and let tools format it.
Quote, paraphrase or summarise with citation; patchwork copying is plagiarism; similarity scores screen, humans judge; disclose and verify AI assistance.

units.title: Visual Communication - Tables, Charts, Diagrams and Slides
topics: Seeing the ideas: honest axes, chart choice and contrast

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: honest axes, chart choice and contrast

summary: Choose the medium by purpose: tables for exact values, charts for patterns, diagrams for structure; every graphic is referred to, numbered, captioned and self-explanatory.
Chart type follows the question; bars start at zero; the lie factor measures distortion (a truncated bar chart showing 5% as 100% has a lie factor of 20.0).
Never rely on colour alone; WCAG contrast needs 4.5:1 for body text; #999999 on white gives 2.85:1 and fails.
Diagrams carry one message with consistent notation; slides carry one idea with a headline sentence.

units.title: Editing, Professional Communication and Ethics
topics: Reports, minutes, CVs and cover letters
Seeing the ideas: the four edits, the handwritten letter and the first meeting

sections.title: Reports, minutes, CVs and cover letters
Seeing the ideas: the four edits, the handwritten letter and the first meeting

summary: Edit in levels (substantive, copy, proofread, technical) from large to small; use a checklist, rest, read aloud and verify every number.
Scripted replacements remove deadwood: the sample paragraph fell from 44 to 22 words (50.0% shorter); a human must still review them.
Emails need an action-oriented subject, the main point first and a clear next step; minutes record decisions and owned actions; CVs show measurable results.
Ethical communication is honest, credits sources, protects confidentiality, warns of risk and is accessible.

units.title: Writing for the Web, Information Reports, Proposals and Group Work
summary: Team writing works when roles, a style sheet and a single master copy are fixed in advance and reviews happen in rounds.
Web readers scan, so pages put the answer first, use headings and lists, and give links and images descriptive text.
Information reports (abstracts, mechanism and process descriptions, periodic and progress reports, news releases) present facts in a fixed form for a defined reader.
Proposals persuade with specific objectives, a plan, a schedule and a budget that adds up.
A group presentation needs one message, divided topics, planned hand-offs and joint rehearsal.

units.title: Instructions, Technical Descriptions and Formal Reports
topics: Report checklist and ethics of reporting

sections.title: Report checklist and ethics of reporting

summary: Instructions tell a reader how to act, so they need a verb-led title, requirements, notices before steps, one action per step, a stated result and a troubleshooting table, and they must be tested with a first-time user.
A formal definition names the class and the differentia; an extended definition adds methods such as examples, analogy, classification and process.
A description of a mechanism pictures an object by parts in a fixed spatial order with exact measurements; a process description uses time order.
A formal report has front matter, body and back matter; the abstract or executive summary and letter of transmittal are written last, and the body separates findings, conclusions and recommendations.
Recommendation and feasibility reports rest on stated criteria, a transparent decision matrix, costs that add up and a sensitivity check; honesty about uncertainty is a professional duty.
